coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, and the app's riskiest logic — filtering, pagination, URL state, sorting, and the request-time cache — is entirely unguarded. Even the pure helpers in lib/format.ts, which are trivially unit-testable, have no coverage.

evidence: app/ — no test files, so no padding and no maintenance burden
signal_to_noise.rationale: Per the rubric, no tests scores 3: there is no noise, but also no signal.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure whatsoever: no test script, no runner (vitest/playwright) in devDependencies, no test files anywhere under app/src. Every behavior is guarded only by the acceptance suite in tests/, which the team does not own as a regression net.
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight unit runner (vitest needs no browser) and a `test` script; start with the pure helpers, which need no server or DOM.

findings.issue: cardsFor does the highest-stakes data transformation in the app — alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000), dedupe of a Pokémon that can appear twice in a list, species-name resolution, and dex-number ordering — with no tests.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests over fixture refs: Mega form excluded, duplicate id kept once, unsorted input comes out dex-ordered, unknown id skipped.

findings.issue: URL filter state is the most fragile code in the repo: readFilters/toQuery (omit-empty/default params, page=1 reset on filter change), plus a 150 ms debounce coordinated through a lastWritten ref and a dependency-less effect. A refactor that adds a dependency array to the effect at line 66, or drops the page: 1 reset in the select handlers at lines 108/122, breaks live behavior with no failing test.
findings.suggestion: Extract toQuery/readFilters and test them as pure functions (round-trip defaults, q trimming, page omission at 1); add a component test that typing then changing a select lands on page 1 with the right query string.

findings.issue: The sortable-table contract is subtle and untested: missing values must sort last in BOTH directions (the missingA/missingB branch at line 66 is easy to invert), a second click must flip direction, aria-sort must move with the sorted header, and compareMethods must order level-up/machine/egg/tutor then alphabetical.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test compareValues/compareMethods and the sort comparator with nulls mixed into power/accuracy; assert missing-last holds for dir: 'descending' too.

findings.issue: The humanize/dexNumber/orMissing/latestEnglishFlavorText helpers define user-visible output for every page (Mr Mime, #0025, —, \n/\f collapsing) and are pure and trivially testable, yet untested.
findings.suggestion: A 20-line unit test file covering humanize('mr-mime'), dexNumber(25), orMissing(null), and a flavor entry containing 'POKéMON\fMONSTER' style whitespace.

findings.issue: The runtime cache and URL re-rooting are untested and edge-heavy: prune() mixes expiry and insertion-order eviction; rejected promises are only evicted if still the current entry (line 53); 404 NotFoundError promises are negatively cached for the full 30 s TTL, so a resource that appears upstream can keep 404ing; the indexOf('/api/v2/') re-root silently corrupts paths that don't contain that prefix (slice(7) of an unrelated absolute URL).
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a stubbed fetch: 404-then-success within TTL, cache hit avoiding a second fetch, and re-rooting of an absolute API URL. Consider not caching NotFoundError promises at all.

findings.issue: getMoves builds the Game/learn data and relies on groupRecords.sort by order plus games.at(-1) as the default selection (MovesSection.tsx:103); a stable-sort or ordering regression silently changes which game the tables open on.
findings.suggestion: A test that, given two version groups with orders 10 and 20, the select defaults to the order-20 group and ?game= overrides it.

findings.issue: Route-name normalization (decodeURIComponent + toLowerCase, repeated in all four [name] pages) is copy-pasted and untested; double-encoded or cased URLs (/pokemon/Mr.%20Mime, /types/FIRE) depend on it for the 404-vs-found decision.
findings.suggestion: Extract one normalizeRouteName() helper into lib/format.ts and unit-test encode/decode round trips.

findings.issue: The home index is assembled by cross-joining 18 type records and 9 generation records by pokemon-species id, including slot ordering and the id > MAX_SPECIES_ID filter; nothing pins that a species with a single type in slot 2 (or a species missing from every generation list) is handled by the ?? '' fallback at line 41.
findings.suggestion: Extract the index-building loop into a testable function and cover: empty type list for a species, slot-2-only type, alternate-form entry in type.data.pokemon.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own — no runner, no test script, no test files — so the app's entire behavioral surface is guarded only by the acceptance suite it was handed. That is a real cost for a codebase someone will own for years: the riskiest logic (URL filter state with its debounced lastWritten-ref dance, the sortable moves tables, cardsFor's alternate-form filtering, and the TTL cache) is exactly the code a refactor would break silently. The pure helpers in lib/format.ts and lib/cards.ts are one afternoon of vitest away from solid coverage and would be the first thing I'd ask for in review.
